claims.text: Grants are available for works-in-progress in fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and script projects.
Grants can be used for research, travel, or other expenditures.
Grants are awarded in addition to any publisher's advance.
The Authors’ Foundation fund is open to writers who have been previously published or have a contract for their project with a commercial UK publisher or producer.
Grants are usually between £2,000-£3,000.
There are no deadlines for this fund as it accepts submissions on a rolling basis.

For book projects, applicants must have been commissioned by a commercial UK or Irish publisher to write or translate a full-length work of fiction, poetry, or non-fiction and need funding for research, travel, or other expenditure.

Alternatively, for book projects, applicants without a contractual commitment with a publisher must have had at least one book published commercially by a UK or Irish publisher, of which they are the sole author or translator, and there is a strong likelihood that their next book will be published in the UK or Ireland.
In both book project cases, applicants must have a non-contributory contract where the author does not pay funds towards publication costs.
For script projects, applicants must have previously had a work of which they are the sole author professionally performed on stage, screen, or radio in the UK or Ireland.
Alternatively, for script projects, applicants must be currently under contract to write a script that will be professionally performed on stage, screen, or radio in the UK or Ireland.
Hybrid and self-published books are not eligible for the funds.
Grants cannot be awarded to cover publication, promotion, or production costs.
Grants cannot fund student tuition fees.
Grants are only awarded for one work-in-progress.
Editors are not eligible to apply.
Applications for AI generated works are not accepted.
No author may apply to the same assessor panel twice.
Applicants who have previously received a K Blundell Trust Award or Author’s Foundation grant must wait four years before re-applying to the fund.
The Authors’ Foundation accepts submissions for fiction, non-fiction, poetry, and script projects.
The Authors’ Foundation was set up from donations by authors in 1984.
The Authors’ Foundation has received contributions from authors, charitable trusts, and the Royal Literary Fund.
The Society of Authors is one of the few organisations that awards grants to writers for works-in-progress.
The Authors’ Foundation, K Blundell Trust, and Arthur Welton Foundation currently award over £360,000 each year.
Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.
To apply, download the form and submit it to grants@societyofauthors.org.
There may be a wait of up to five months for a decision on an application to the Authors’ Foundation.
If a grant application is successful, payment will usually be made within 10 working days of the SoA receiving payment information.
The Eric Ambler Awards are for a spy novel or thriller.
The Taner Baybars Awards offer funding for original fiction in the fields of science fiction, fantasy, and magic realism.
The John Brooks Awards offer funding to writers based in the West Country or Wales.
The Antonia Fraser Grants are for a biography of a woman or women.
The Arthur Welton Awards are generally awarded to poets.
The Great Britain Sasakawa Grant of £2,000 is awarded annually for works of fiction or non-fiction about any aspect of Japanese culture or society, or set in a Japanese context.
The Authors’ Foundation is a registered charity in England and Wales (charity number 326605).
The Arthur Welton Foundation is a registered charity in England and Wales (charity number 282446).
